            The 'General Use (Light)' model is the original model used in the BiRefNet repository.
            The 'General Use (Light 2K)' model is the original model used in the BiRefNet repository but trained with 2K images.
            The 'General Use (Heavy)' model is a slower but more accurate model.
            The 'Matting' model is a model trained specifically for matting images.
            The 'Portrait' model is a model trained specifically for portrait images.
            The 'General Use (Dynamic)' model supports dynamic resolutions from 256x256 to 2304x2304.
            The 'General Use (Light)' model is recommended for most use cases.

            The corresponding models are as follows:
            - 'General Use (Light)': BiRefNet

            - 'General Use (Heavy)': BiRefNet_lite

docstring: Smart image resize to arbitrary dimensions, powered by Nano Banana Pro with vision-LLM-guided prompting for composition-aware recomposition. Crop, cropping, resize ads.

inputFields.name: safety_tolerance
inputFields.description: The safety tolerance level applied to the inner nano-banana-pro /edit calls. Higher numbers loosen safety filtering.

inputFields.name: num_images_per_size
inputFields.description: The number of nano-banana-pro variants to produce for each target size. The response images list will contain ``len(target_sizes) * num_images_per_size`` images in total.

inputFields.name: output_format
inputFields.description: The output image format.

inputFields.name: target_sizes
inputFields.description: The list of target dimensions to generate, each written as ``<width>x<height>`` (e.g. ``"1920x1080"``). One output image is produced per target size (multiplied by ``num_images_per_size``). The endpoint internally picks the smallest nano-banana-pro preset that fully covers each target so the final image is a pixel-perfect match with no upscaling.

inputFields.name: image
inputFields.description: The URL of the source image to resize.

inputFields.name: seed
inputFields.description: Optional random seed forwarded to the inner nano-banana-pro /edit calls for reproducibility. The same seed is used for every target size when set.

inputFields.name: prompt
inputFields.description: Optional extra instruction that is forwarded to nano-banana-pro alongside the auto-generated resize prompt. Leave empty to let the model preserve the original image content as closely as possible.

inputFields.name: sync_mode
inputFields.description: When True, the response contains data URIs in place of CDN URLs so the client can decode the images without an extra HTTP request. Adds latency for large outputs.

inputFields.name: resolution
inputFields.description: Hint for the minimum resolution tier to use internally. The smart-resize algorithm may pick a higher tier automatically when the requested target size is too large for this tier. This field does not affect the final output dimensions — those come from ``target_sizes``.

outputFields.name: description
outputFields.description: The description of the generated images.

outputFields.name: results
outputFields.description: Per-target-size breakdown with the requested width/height and the nano-banana-pro (aspect_ratio, resolution) preset that was used internally.

outputFields.name: images
outputFields.description: All generated images, flattened across every target size. Order matches the order of ``results`` below: the first ``num_images_per_size`` entries correspond to ``target_sizes[0]`` and so on.

enums.name: SafetyTolerance
enums.description: The safety tolerance level applied to the inner nano-banana-pro /edit calls. Higher numbers loosen safety filtering.

enums.name: OutputFormat
enums.description: The output image format.

inputFields.name: shape_slat_guidance_strength
inputFields.description: How closely the detailed geometry follows the input image. Higher values add more detail but may introduce noise.

inputFields.name: uv_unwrap_global_iterations
inputFields.description: Number of global clustering passes during UV chart computation. More passes produce more balanced charts.

inputFields.name: shape_slat_guidance_rescale
inputFields.description: Dampens artifacts from high guidance in the shape stage. Increase if you see noisy geometry.

inputFields.name: uv_unwrap_refine_iterations
inputFields.description: Number of local refinement passes during UV chart computation. Higher values produce cleaner chart boundaries at the cost of additional UV-unwrap time.

inputFields.name: ss_guidance_interval_end
inputFields.description: Fraction of the denoising process at which classifier-free guidance ends for stage 1 (sparse structure). Must be >= ss_guidance_interval_start.

inputFields.name: texture_size
inputFields.description: Resolution of the texture image baked onto the mesh. Higher values capture finer surface details but produce larger files.

inputFields.name: tex_slat_guidance_interval_start
inputFields.description: Fraction of the denoising process at which classifier-free guidance starts for stage 3 (texture). Guidance is only applied between interval_start and interval_end.

inputFields.name: seed
inputFields.description: Random seed for reproducibility

inputFields.name: ss_guidance_rescale
inputFields.description: Dampens artifacts from high guidance in stage 1. Lower values allow stronger guidance effects, higher values stabilize the output.

inputFields.name: ss_sampling_steps
inputFields.description: Number of denoising steps for the initial structure. More steps = slower but potentially higher quality.

inputFields.name: decimation_target
inputFields.description: Target number of vertices in the final mesh. Lower values produce smaller files but less detail. 500k is good for most uses, reduce to 20k-50k for web/mobile.

inputFields.name: tex_slat_sampling_steps
inputFields.description: Number of denoising steps for texture generation. More steps = slower but potentially cleaner textures.

inputFields.name: ss_guidance_strength
inputFields.description: How closely the initial 3D structure follows the input image. Higher values produce more faithful but potentially noisier results.

inputFields.name: tex_slat_guidance_strength
inputFields.description: How closely the texture follows the input image colors. Higher values produce more vivid but potentially oversaturated textures.

inputFields.name: shape_slat_guidance_interval_start
inputFields.description: Fraction of the denoising process at which classifier-free guidance starts for stage 2 (shape refinement). Guidance is only applied between interval_start and interval_end.

inputFields.name: ss_guidance_interval_start
inputFields.description: Fraction of the denoising process at which classifier-free guidance starts for stage 1 (sparse structure). Guidance is only applied between interval_start and interval_end; outside this window the model runs unguided. Lower values apply guidance earlier.

inputFields.name: shape_slat_guidance_interval_end
inputFields.description: Fraction of the denoising process at which classifier-free guidance ends for stage 2 (shape refinement). Must be >= shape_slat_guidance_interval_start.

inputFields.name: tex_slat_rescale_t
inputFields.description: Controls noise schedule sharpness for texture generation. Higher values produce sharper texture details.

inputFields.name: remesh_project
inputFields.description: How much to project remeshed vertices back onto the original surface. 0 = no projection (smoother), 1 = full projection (preserves detail).

inputFields.name: ss_rescale_t
inputFields.description: Controls noise schedule sharpness for structure generation. Higher values produce sharper transitions.

inputFields.name: shape_slat_rescale_t
inputFields.description: Controls noise schedule sharpness for shape refinement. Higher values produce sharper geometric details.

inputFields.name: uv_unwrap_smooth_strength
inputFields.description: Smoothing strength applied to UV chart boundaries. Higher values reduce visible seams but may introduce UV distortion.

inputFields.name: tex_slat_guidance_rescale
inputFields.description: Dampens artifacts from high guidance in the texture stage. Increase if textures look noisy or have color banding.

inputFields.name: tex_slat_guidance_interval_end
inputFields.description: Fraction of the denoising process at which classifier-free guidance ends for stage 3 (texture). Must be >= tex_slat_guidance_interval_start.

inputFields.name: shape_slat_sampling_steps
inputFields.description: Number of denoising steps for shape refinement. More steps = slower but potentially smoother geometry.

inputFields.name: remesh_band
inputFields.description: Controls how far remeshing can move vertices from the original surface. Higher values allow more smoothing but may lose fine details.

inputFields.name: resolution
inputFields.description: Output resolution; higher is slower but more detailed

inputFields.name: remesh
inputFields.description: Rebuild the mesh topology for cleaner triangles. Slower but usually produces better results for downstream use (animation, 3D printing, etc).

inputFields.name: image
inputFields.description: URL of the input image to convert to 3D

inputFields.name: uv_unwrap_angle_threshold_deg
inputFields.description: Maximum angle (in degrees) between adjacent face normals allowed within a single UV chart. Lower values produce more charts with less distortion; higher values produce fewer, larger charts with potentially more stretching.

inputFields.description: Texture generation quality. When unset, the API picks a default appropriate for the tier.

inputFields.description: URL of images to use while generating the 3D model. Required for Image-to-3D mode. Up to 5 images allowed.

inputFields.description: Material type. PBR: physically-based materials with realistic lighting. Shaded: baked lighting with no PBR maps. All: both PBR and Shaded variants. None: geometry only with no textures.

inputFields.description: This is a controlnet that controls the maximum sized of the generated model.

inputFields.name: tier
inputFields.description: Generation tier. Higher tiers produce more detailed meshes but cost more. Extreme-High enables the highest-detail mode and bills at double the base rate. See more info in the [documentation](https://developer.hyper3d.ai/api-specification/rodin-gen2.5#use-gen-2.5-generation-with-following-gen-2.5-tiers). Selecting Gen-2.5-Minimum will automatically configure to a minimum mode, where 50K Triangle is selected, taking priority over quality_mesh_option.

inputFields.description: If enabled, the generation will have enhanced generative robustness while ensuring output consistency. This corresponds to `geometry_instruct_mode` being equal to `creative` on the Hyper3D API.

inputFields.description: Generate a preview render image of the 3D model along with the model files.

inputFields.name: texture_delight
inputFields.description: Removes baked lighting/highlights from the generated textures.

inputFields.description: Format of the geometry file. Possible values: glb, usdz, fbx, obj, stl. Default is glb.

inputFields.name: is_micro
inputFields.description: Generate finer micro-scale geometric detail. Only effective with `tier="Gen-2.5-Extreme-High"`.

inputFields.name: seed
inputFields.description: Seed value for randomization, ranging from 0 to 65535. Optional.

inputFields.name: quality_mesh_option
inputFields.description:
Combined quality and mesh type selection. Quad = smooth surfaces, Triangle = detailed geometry. Maps to `mesh_mode` (Quad/Raw) and `quality_override` (face count) on the Hyper3D API. Valid face counts depend on the selected tier. Up to 1M Triangle is supported for tiers Extreme-Low, Low, and Medium. Up to 2M Triangle (as low as 20K Triangle) is supported for tiers High and Extreme-High. Auto option will choose the advised options for each tier:
1. Gen-2.5-Minimum: 50K Triangle
2. Gen-2.5-Extreme-Low: 50K Triangle
3. Gen-2.5-Low: 50K Triangle
4. Gen-2.5-Medium: 500K Triangle
5. Gen-2.5-High: 500K Triangle
Gen-2.5-Extreme-High: 1M Triangle.

inputFields.name: hd_texture
inputFields.description: Enables enhanced texture post-processing for higher visual fidelity.

inputFields.name: use_original_alpha
inputFields.description: When enabled, preserves the transparency channel from input images during 3D generation.

outputFields.name: model_meshes
outputFields.description: Additional generated 3D object files returned by Hyper3D besides model_mesh.

inputFields.default: The video captures a series of frames showing macroblocking artifacts, chromatic aberration, high-frequency noise, and rolling shutter distortion. It includes static with no motion, motion blur, over-saturation, shaky footage, low resolution, grainy texture, pixelated images, poorly lit areas, underexposed and overexposed scenes, poor color balance, washed out colors, choppy sequences, jerky movements, low frame rate, bit-depth compression artifacts, color banding, unnatural transitions, outdated special effects, fake elements, unconvincing visuals, poorly edited content, jump cuts, hard cut, visual noise, and flickering. It features moiré patterns, edge halos, and temporal aliasing. Furthermore, the content defies common sense, generating illogical scenarios, nonsensical entities, absurd character behaviors, and conceptual paradoxes that violate basic human reasoning and everyday reality. The video looks like a surreal or glitchy hallucination. Overall, the video is of poor quality.

1. Gen-2.5-Minimum: 50K Triangle

3. Gen-2.5-Low: 50K Triangle
4. Gen-2.5-Medium: 500K Triangle
5. Gen-2.5-High: 500K Triangle
Gen-2.5-Extreme-High: 1M Triangle.

inputFields.name: tier

See more info in the [documentation](https://developer.hyper3d.ai/api-specification/rodin-gen2.5#use-gen-2.5-generation-with-following-gen-2.5-tiers). Selecting Gen-2.5-Minimum will automatically configure to a minimum mode, where 50K Triangle is selected, taking priority over quality_mesh_option.

inputFields.description: Optional style and delivery instructions prepended to the prompt. Controls expressiveness, accent, pace, tone, and emotional expression using natural language. Examples: 'Speak warmly and slowly', 'Read this as a dramatic newscast', 'Use a British accent with a cheerful tone', 'Whisper mysteriously'.

inputFields.name: temperature
inputFields.description: Controls the randomness of the speech output. Higher values produce more creative and varied delivery, while lower values make the output more predictable and focused.

inputFields.description: Language for multilingual synthesis. When set, steers the model to speak in the specified language. Supports 24 GA languages and 60+ Preview languages. If not set, the model auto-detects the language from the text.

inputFields.name: voice
inputFields.description: Voice preset for single-speaker synthesis. 30 distinct voices are available. Ignored when speakers is set. inputFields.name: prompt
inputFields.description: The text to convert to speech. Gemini TTS supports natural-language prompting for style, pace, accent, and emotional expression — include delivery instructions inline with the text (e.g. 'Say cheerfully: Have a wonderful day!'). For multi-speaker synthesis, prefix lines with speaker aliases defined in the speakers field (e.g. 'Alice: Hello!\nBob: Hi!'). Supports inline pace/style markers like [slowly], [whispering], [excited], [extremely fast].

docstring: Gemini 3.1 Flash text-to-speech.

inputFields.name: style_instructions
inputFields.description: Optional style and delivery instructions prepended to the prompt. Controls expressiveness, accent, pace, tone, and emotional expression using natural language. Use this to separate style control from the text content. Examples: 'Speak warmly and slowly', 'Read this as a dramatic newscast', 'Use a British accent with a cheerful tone', 'Whisper mysteriously'.

inputFields.name: output_format
inputFields.description: Audio output format. mp3: compressed, small file size (recommended). wav: uncompressed PCM wrapped in WAV (24 kHz, 16-bit mono). ogg_opus: Ogg container with Opus codec, good quality-to-size ratio.

inputFields.name: language_code
inputFields.description: Language for multilingual synthesis. When set, steers the model to speak in the specified language. If not set, the model auto-detects the language from the text.

inputFields.name: temperature
inputFields.description: Controls the randomness of the speech output. Higher values produce more creative and varied delivery, while lower values make the output more predictable and focused.

inputFields.name: speakers
inputFields.description: Multi-speaker voice configuration. When set, enables multi-speaker synthesis where different parts of the text are spoken by different voices. Each speaker needs a voice and a speaker_id (alias) that matches prefixes in the prompt.

inputFields.name: voice
inputFields.description: Voice preset for single-speaker synthesis. 30 distinct voices are available. Ignored when speakers is set. Popular choices: Kore (strong, firm female), Puck (upbeat, lively male), Charon (calm, professional male), Zephyr (bright, clear female), Aoede (warm, melodic female).

inputFields.name: prompt
inputFields.description: The text to convert to speech. Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS supports natural-language prompting for style, pace, accent, and emotional expression — include delivery instructions inline with the text (e.g. 'Say cheerfully: Have a wonderful day!'). Supports expressive audio tags like [sigh], [laughing], [whispering], [short pause] for fine-grained control over delivery. For multi-speaker synthesis, prefix lines with speaker aliases defined in the speakers field (e.g. 'Alice: Hello!\nBob: Hi!').

enums.name: OutputFormat

inputFields.description:
URL of the audio to use as the background music. Must be publicly accessible.
Limit handling: If the audio duration exceeds the duration value (5 or 10 seconds),
the audio is truncated to the first 5 or 10 seconds, and the rest is discarded. If
the audio is shorter than the video, the remaining part of the video will be silent.
For example, if the audio is 3 seconds long and the video duration is 5 seconds, the
first 3 seconds of the output video will have sound, and the last 2 seconds will be silent.
- Format: WAV, MP3.
- Duration: 3 to 30 s.
- File size: Up to 15 MB.

inputFields.description: If true, the number of frames per second will be multiplied by the number of interpolated frames plus one. inputFields.name: split_input_into_scenes
inputFields.description: If true, videos above a certain duration threshold will be split into scenes.

inputFields.name: audio_preserve_pitch
inputFields.description: When audio duration doesn't match video duration, stretch/compress audio without changing pitch. If disabled, audio is trimmed or padded with silence.

inputFields.name: validation
inputFields.description: A list of validation prompts to use during training. When providing an image, _all_ validation inputs must have an image.

inputFields.name: validation_number_of_frames
inputFields.description: The number of frames in validation videos.

inputFields.name: trigger_phrase
inputFields.description: A phrase that will trigger the LoRA style. Will be prepended to captions during training.

inputFields.name: with_audio
inputFields.description: Enable joint audio-video training. If None (default), automatically detects whether input videos have audio. Set to True to force audio training, or False to disable.

inputFields.name: validation_frame_rate
inputFields.description: Target frames per second for validation videos.

inputFields.name: aspect_ratio
inputFields.description: Aspect ratio to use for training.

inputFields.name: training_data_url
inputFields.description:
URL to zip archive with videos or images. Try to use at least 10 files, although more is better.

        **Supported video formats:** .mp4, .mov, .avi, .mkv
        **Supported image formats:** .png, .jpg, .jpeg

        Note: The dataset must contain ONLY videos OR ONLY images - mixed datasets are not supported.

        The archive can also contain text files with captions. Each text file should have the same name as the media file it corresponds to.

inputFields.name: number_of_steps
inputFields.description: The number of training steps.

inputFields.name: learning_rate
inputFields.description: Learning rate for optimization. Higher values can lead to faster training but may cause overfitting.

inputFields.name: frame_rate
inputFields.description: Target frames per second for the video.

inputFields.name: validation_aspect_ratio
inputFields.description: The aspect ratio to use for validation.

inputFields.name: number_of_frames
inputFields.description: Number of frames per training sample. Must satisfy frames % 8 == 1 (e.g., 1, 9, 17, 25, 33, 41, 49, 57, 65, 73, 81, 89, 97).

inputFields.name: first_frame_conditioning_p
inputFields.description: Probability of conditioning on the first frame during training. Higher values improve image-to-video performance.

inputFields.name: generate_audio_in_validation
inputFields.description: Whether to generate audio in validation samples.

inputFields.name: validation_negative_prompt
inputFields.default: worst quality, inconsistent motion, blurry, jittery, distorted
inputFields.description: A negative prompt to use for validation.

inputFields.name: validation_resolution
inputFields.description: The resolution to use for validation.

inputFields.name: audio_normalize
inputFields.description: Normalize audio peak amplitude to a consistent level. Recommended for consistent audio levels across the dataset.

inputFields.name: resolution
inputFields.description: Resolution to use for training. Higher resolutions require more memory.

inputFields.name: stg_scale
inputFields.description: STG (Spatio-Temporal Guidance) scale. 0.0 disables STG. Recommended value is 1.0.

inputFields.name: split_input_duration_threshold
inputFields.description: The duration threshold in seconds. If a video is longer than this, it will be split into scenes.

inputFields.name: rank
inputFields.description: The rank of the LoRA adaptation. Higher values increase capacity but use more memory.

inputFields.name: auto_scale_input
inputFields.description: If true, videos will be automatically scaled to the target frame count and fps. This option has no effect on image datasets.

inputFields.name: debug_dataset
inputFields.description: When enabled, the trainer returns a downloadable archive of your preprocessed training data for manual inspection. Use this to verify that your videos, images, and captions were processed correctly before committing to a full training run.

outputFields.name: config_file
outputFields.description: Configuration used for setting up inference endpoints.

outputFields.name: debug_dataset
outputFields.description: A downloadable archive containing the preprocessed training data, including decoded videos and audio. Only present when `debug_dataset` is enabled in the input.

outputFields.name: video
outputFields.description: The URL to the validation videos, if any.

outputFields.name: lora_file
outputFields.description: URL to the trained LoRA weights (.safetensors).

docstring: Qwen Image Layered Trainer

inputFields.name: learning_rate
inputFields.description: Learning rate for LoRA parameters.

inputFields.name: steps
inputFields.description: Number of steps to train for

inputFields.name: image_data
inputFields.description:
URL to the input data zip archive.

    The zip should contain groups of images. The images should be named:

    ROOT_start.EXT, ROOT_end.EXT, ROOT_end2.EXT, ..., ROOT_endN.EXT
    For example:
    photo_start.png, photo_end.png, photo_end2.png, ..., photo_endN.png

    The start image is the base image that will be decomposed into layers.
    The end images are the layers that will be added to the base image.  ROOT_end.EXT is the first layer, ROOT_end2.EXT is the second layer, and so on.
    You can have up to 8 layers.
    All image groups must have the same number of output layers.

    The end images can contain transparent regions. Only PNG and WebP images are supported since these are the only formats that support transparency.

    The zip can also contain a text file for each image group. The text file should be named:
    ROOT.txt
    For example:
    photo.txt

    This text file can be used to specify a description of the base image.

    If no text file is provided, the default_caption will be used.

    If no default_caption is provided, the training will fail.

inputFields.description: Random seed for reproducibility.

inputFields.description: Temporal window size for inference. The backend snaps this to the nearest CogVideoX-safe value that works with temporal compression and patching. Valid outputs are 69, 77, 85, ..., 197.

inputFields.name: quad_mask_video
inputFields.description: URL of a mask video for the removal target. For best results this should be a VOID-style quadmask video with 4 grayscale values: 0=object to remove, 63=overlap, 127=affected region, 255=background to keep. A simple binary mask (0=remove, 255=keep) also works. If omitted, the app will generate a temporary mask video from `mask_prompt` using the SAM-3 video endpoint and convert it to a quadmask automatically.

docstring: Transfer movements from a reference video to any character image. Cost-effective mode for motion transfer, perfect for portraits and simple animations.

inputFields.description: Optional element for facial consistency binding. Upload a facial element to enhance identity preservation in the generated video. Only 1 element is supported. Reference in prompt as @Element1. Element binding is only supported when character_orientation is 'video'.

inputFields.description: Controls whether the output character's orientation matches the reference image or video. 'video': orientation matches reference video - better for complex motions (max 30s). 'image': orientation matches reference image - better for following camera movements (max 10s).

inputFields.description: Whether to keep the original sound from the reference video.

inputFields.description: Reference video URL. The character actions in the generated video will be consistent with this reference video. Duration limit depends on character_orientation: 10s max for 'image', 30s max for 'video'.

inputFields.description: The URL of the source video to transform.

inputFields.description: Whether to include audio in the returned video. When disabled, the final MP4 is returned without an audio track.

inputFields.description: Number of inference steps. Defaults to 15 and can be increased up to 30.

inputFields.name: frames_per_second
inputFields.description: Frames per second of the generated video.

inputFields.name: num_frames
inputFields.description: The number of output frames. Output duration is num_frames / frames_per_second. The IC-LoRA control budget caps the resolution x frames volume: roughly 6s at 720p or 15s at 480p; a request above it returns a 422 (lower num_frames, or use 480p).

inputFields.name: prompt
inputFields.description: Optional short description of the video's content/scene. It is woven into the effect's trained caption to sharpen the result; leave empty to apply the effect with a generic description.

inputFields.name: video_quality
inputFields.description: The quality preset of the generated video.

inputFields.name: resolution
inputFields.description: Output resolution (short side), preserving the source aspect ratio. The IC-LoRA control path caps the resolution x frames volume, so resolution trades against duration: 720p allows up to ~6s (sharper), 480p up to ~15s (softer but longer). A request above the budget is rejected with a clear error — pick 480p for longer clips. Output duration is num_frames / frames_per_second.

docstring: Generate high-quality video with audio from reference video, text and images using LTX-2.3

inputFields.name: mid_image
inputFields.description: Optional middle-frame keyframe image. When set, the look/appearance is anchored to this image around the middle of the clip (in addition to image_url at the start), so the appearance follows a moving camera instead of drifting. Requires image_url.

inputFields.name: control_video
inputFields.description: Optional pre-computed control video (e.g. an already-rendered depth / edge / pose composite). When provided together with skip_control_preprocess, the built-in control estimation is skipped and this video is used directly as the control signal, resampled to the output resolution and frame count.

inputFields.name: video_write_mode
inputFields.description: The write mode of the generated video.

inputFields.name: video
inputFields.description: The URL of the reference video that supplies motion/structure.

inputFields.name: num_inference_steps
inputFields.description: Number of inference steps. Defaults to 15 and can be increased up to 30.

inputFields.name: end_image
inputFields.description: Optional last-frame keyframe image. When set, the look/appearance is anchored to this image at the end of the clip. Useful for shots where the camera travels to a different place than the start image. Requires image_url.

inputFields.name: num_frames
inputFields.description: The number of output frames to generate. This IC-LoRA endpoint caps the resolution x frames volume for stability (~150 frames at 720p-class; more at smaller sizes). A request above the budget returns a 422 — reduce num_frames or use a smaller resolution.

inputFields.name: prompt
inputFields.description: The prompt to guide generation.

inputFields.name: seed
inputFields.description: Random seed for reproducibility. If None, a random seed is chosen.

inputFields.name: resolution
inputFields.description: The size of the generated video. In direct-control mode (skip_control_preprocess with control_video_url), 'auto' follows the source video size/aspect up to the LTX limits and explicit sizes are honored with 64px alignment. In the built-in control estimation mode, the output stays near the official control workflow size. Higher resolutions reduce the maximum stable frame count; lower resolutions can run longer.

inputFields.name: preserve_original_video
inputFields.description: True video-to-video: the base video_url is used as the generation's starting point, while control_video_url still drives the structure. The amount of the original preserved is controlled by `strength` (denoise): lower `strength` keeps more of the original video's pixels. Requires skip_control_preprocess, video_url and control_video_url. Default off leaves the standard control path unchanged.

inputFields.name: skip_control_preprocess
inputFields.description: Skip the built-in control estimation (depth / edge / pose) and use control_video_url directly as the control signal. Requires control_video_url; ignored if it is not set. With resolution='auto', the output follows the source video size/aspect up to the LTX limits. Explicit resolutions are honored and 64-aligned so the RGB video and control video stay matched.

inputFields.name: negative_prompt
inputFields.default: color distortion, overexposure, static, blurry details, subtitles, style, artwork, painting, frame, still, dim overall tone, worst quality, low quality, JPEG compression artifacts, ugly, mutilated, extra fingers, poorly drawn hands, poorly drawn face, deformed, disfigured, malformed limbs, fused fingers, motionless frame, cluttered background, three legs, crowded background, walking backwards
inputFields.description: The negative prompt to steer generation away from.

inputFields.name: enable_safety_checker
inputFields.description: Whether to enable the safety checker.

inputFields.name: strength
inputFields.description: Sampler denoise strength for reference-video-to-video. With preserve_original_video on, this is the video-to-video amount: lower values keep more of the original video's pixels (e.g. 0.5 = keep ~50%), 1.0 fully regenerates. Without preserve_original_video it only trims the denoise schedule.

inputFields.name: generate_audio
inputFields.description: Whether to include audio in the returned video. When disabled, the final MP4 is returned without an audio track.

inputFields.name: guidance_scale
inputFields.description: Classifier-free guidance scale. The default is tuned for fast, high-quality generation.

inputFields.name: enable_prompt_expansion
inputFields.description: Whether to enable prompt expansion.

inputFields.name: frames_per_second
inputFields.description: Frames per second of the generated video.

inputFields.name: image
inputFields.description: Optional reference image for style/character anchoring. This is the FIRST-frame keyframe.

inputFields.name: video_strength
inputFields.description: Video conditioning strength. Lower values give the model more freedom to change the reference video motion/structure.

inputFields.name: sync_mode
inputFields.description: If True, the media is returned as a data URI inline in the response. Useful for short-lived requests and tests.

inputFields.name: video_quality
inputFields.description: The quality preset of the generated video.

docstring: Transform your 3D video render into realistic using first frame with Ltx 2.3

inputFields.name: intensity
inputFields.description: How hard to push the render toward photorealism. 'light' keeps more of the source render's look and motion; 'strong' transforms more aggressively for a more photoreal result; 'strong-v2' is the newest improved adapter (better multi-scene coherence, audio, talking characters, and higher overall quality).

inputFields.name: video_write_mode
inputFields.description: The write mode of the generated video.

inputFields.name: video
inputFields.description: The URL of the 3D / CG / game render to make photorealistic.

inputFields.name: num_inference_steps
inputFields.description: Number of inference steps. Defaults to 15 and can be increased up to 30.

inputFields.name: enable_detail_refine
inputFields.description: Add a second refinement stage for a sharper, higher-resolution result. After the base pass the video latent is 2x latent-upscaled (spatial upscaler) and refined by a short detailer pass on the distilled model. NOTE: this doubles the output width AND height (4x the pixels), so the request costs roughly 4X THE PRICE and is slower. Off by default.

inputFields.name: num_frames
inputFields.description: The number of output frames. Output duration is num_frames / frames_per_second. The IC-LoRA control budget caps the resolution x frames volume: roughly 6s at 720p or 15s at 480p; a request above it returns a 422 (lower num_frames, or use 480p).

inputFields.name: prompt
inputFields.description: The text prompt, pre-filled with the `3DREAL` trigger the adapter activates on. Describe the photorealistic result after it. The `3DREAL` trigger is always kept, even if you clear it or enable prompt expansion.

inputFields.name: seed
inputFields.description: Random seed for reproducibility. If None, a random seed is chosen.

inputFields.name: resolution
inputFields.description: Output resolution (short side), preserving the source aspect ratio. The IC-LoRA control path caps the resolution x frames volume, so resolution trades against duration: 720p allows up to ~6s (sharper), 480p up to ~15s (softer but longer). A request above the budget is rejected with a clear error — pick 480p for longer clips. Output duration is num_frames / frames_per_second.

inputFields.name: negative_prompt
inputFields.default: color distortion, overexposure, static, blurry details, subtitles, style, artwork, painting, frame, still, dim overall tone, worst quality, low quality, JPEG compression artifacts, ugly, mutilated, extra fingers, poorly drawn hands, poorly drawn face, deformed, disfigured, malformed limbs, fused fingers, motionless frame, cluttered background, three legs, crowded background, walking backwards
inputFields.description: The negative prompt to steer generation away from.

inputFields.name: enable_prompt_expansion
inputFields.description: When enabled, an AI model expands your prompt into a richer description before generation (off by default sends it as written). The `3DREAL` trigger is always kept, and the final prompt used is returned in the output.

inputFields.name: enable_safety_checker
inputFields.description: Whether to enable the safety checker.

inputFields.name: generate_audio

inputFields.name: frames_per_second
inputFields.description: Frames per second of the generated video.

inputFields.name: image
inputFields.description: Optional reference image used as the FIRST frame (image-to-video anchor), matching how the adapter was trained. It defines the photoreal look of frame 0; leave empty to let the render alone drive the result.

inputFields.name: sync_mode
inputFields.description: If True, the media is returned as a data URI inline in the response. Useful for short-lived requests and tests.

inputFields.name: detail_refine_strength
inputFields.description: Denoise strength of the detailer pass, used only when enable_detail_refine is on. Higher regenerates more detail (and can drift further from the base); lower is a lighter touch that stays closer to the base. Default 0.75.
